long_biography.plain_text:
Software entrepreneurship established Ron Zuckerman's career. He co-founded Sapiens International, served as its chief operating officer, and later became chairman and chief executive. The insurance-software company went public on Nasdaq in 1990. He also founded Precise Software Solutions and served as its executive chairman, guiding the application-performance software business through a Nasdaq flotation before its 2003 acquisition by Veritas. The acquisition's reported value was a company transaction, not a measure of Zuckerman's personal proceeds.

Zuckerman broadened that operating record into technology investing. He was an early investor and director at several software and telecommunications businesses and participated in venture funds including Magma Venture Partners, Raine and Compound. A current advisory biography describes more than 35 years in high technology and involvement with over 120 startups. His identifiable present activity is therefore investment-led, while the fortune's documented origin remains the software companies he founded and brought to public markets.
